aspect: The information belongs to somebody else
description: A contractor placed through an agency frequently does not know the end client's legal name, address or supervision structure, and the agency may be contractually barred from disclosing it. Not knowing is a correct professional answer and reads as evasion.
energy_note: The honest answer is 'I am not allowed to know that'.

aspect: Third-party placement is treated as a red flag in itself
description: Signals of scrutiny include a role appearing too junior for professional level and below-market compensation - both of which are ordinary features of agency contracting rather than evidence of anything.
energy_note: Normal employment structures, read as suspicious.

aspect: The applicant cannot prepare because the question is not published
description: There is no list of what will be asked. The applicant learns what the questions are by failing to answer them.
energy_note: An exam whose syllabus is the transcript of your refusal.

description: He is employed by a firm in Toronto, billed to a client he has signed an NDA about, working on a project that has not been publicly announced. The officer asks where he will physically sit on Monday. He does not know; the allocation happens in the first week. The refusal cites inability to describe the position.
energy_note: Refused for not knowing something that is not yet true.
